edges.qualification: Proposed design requirements; no uptake effect estimated.

scope.configuration: 1989 remote heterogeneous CERN information-management design.

alternatives: Local-only hypertext or homogeneous systems for narrower tasks
edges.dispute: Design feasibility is not observed diffusion contribution.

edges.qualification: Access to existing information was intended to lower migration demands.

scope.configuration: CERN 1989 linking existing information instead of complete replacement.

edges.dispute: No comparative deployment cost study inspected.

edges.qualification: Legal permission for reuse is documented; wider diffusion effect underdetermined.

scope.configuration: Specific released CERN client/server/library components, 1993–1994.

edges.dispute: Retrospective participant account; original signed document not acquired.

edges.qualification: Hypothesised active task complementarity; survey establishes only household coexistence.

scope.configuration: US 2015 ACS computer and handheld access in the same households.

edges.dispute: No within-person task logs or retention/disposal data.

edges.qualification: Alternative internet-access devices for respondents; no estimated substitution elasticity.

scope.configuration: UK internet users 16+ selecting most-important device in 2015.

edges.dispute: Importance does not identify actual task volumes or price differences.

edges.qualification: Tablet and smartphone can serve overlapping internet tasks; many households can retain both.

scope.configuration: UK 2015 device choice, with age-specific alternatives.

edges.dispute: No causal claim that tablet ownership reduced phone adoption.

edges.qualification: Insufficient affordability is the respondent-attributed reason for past suspensions; not a price experiment.

scope.configuration: US 2014 users with no home broadband and few alternative routes online.

edges.dispute: Confounded with other financial hardship; no fixed recall window.

edges.qualification: Perceived comparative difficulty supports task-specific alternatives, not general market dominance.

scope.configuration: UK 2023 forms/documents on smartphone versus laptop/desktop.

edges.dispute: Perceptions, not observed task speed or causal adoption determinant.

edges.qualification: Phone presence permits a route to study but is visibly insufficient for every child.

scope.configuration: ASER 2021 enrolled rural children in homes with smartphones.

edges.dispute: No measured learning outcome; phone-reachable sample excludes some non-exposure.

edges.qualification: Limited child access to the available phone constrains study through that device.

scope.configuration: ASER 2021 conditional child-study access, not all educational participation.

edges.dispute: Reported no/partial access does not identify the source of control restriction or quantify causal learning effects.

edges.qualification: SMS-based implementation did not require smartphone internet.

scope.configuration: Early Kenyan M-PESA transfer instruction/account system.

edges.dispute: Applies to this implementation; later app products may use different inputs.

edges.qualification: Carrier operation supports sending instructions; network outages appear in reported delays.

scope.configuration: Early M-PESA service operation and 2008/2009 reported experience.

edges.dispute: Delay data do not separately identify network versus agent contribution to diffusion.

edges.qualification: Immediate cash payout at the particular agent requires sufficient physical cash there.

scope.configuration: Cash redemption at a specified M-PESA agent in 2008–2009; not electronic transfers generally.

alternatives: Visit another liquid agent, changing the specified location
Spend electronic balance directly, changing the task
edges.necessity_rationale: Without enough cash at the specified payout point, that agent cannot make the specified immediate physical-cash payout; reported shortage delays corroborate the constraint.
edges.dispute: Necessity is task/location-bounded, not a claim that every use of mobile money requires cash-out.

edges.qualification: Registration/ID is part of the early documented account institution.

scope.configuration: Early M-PESA registered accounts described in the 2011 working paper.

alternatives: Existing bank services subject to their own eligibility
edges.dispute: Institutional rules can change; no necessity claim for all money transfers or present-day rules.

edges.qualification: Bank-held funds and agent banking links belong to early implementation; no universal banking architecture claimed.

scope.configuration: Kenyan M-PESA funds/agent structure described in 2011 working paper.

edges.dispute: Not a current-regulation statement or proof that this arrangement alone caused trust.

edges.qualification: Matched survey measures gaming routes; coexistence and different games remain possible.

scope.configuration: UK adults 16+ gaming-device choices, 27 Sep–12 Nov 2023.

edges.dispute: No substitution elasticity, common game catalogue or fixed activity window.

edges.qualification: Adverse prolonged-use experience belongs to the tested hardware/interface bundle.

scope.configuration: Quest 2/remote desktop/K830 configuration, five 8-hour workdays, university worker sample.

edges.dispute: Individual wearing, novelty, display and input effects not separately identified; small sample.

edges.qualification: The physical setup was the experimental comparison for participants’ ordinary work.

scope.configuration: Counterbalanced week in each matched desktop configuration.

edges.dispute: The chosen comparator suppresses possible VR spatial advantages; not all VR work.
